subject: Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees — measurement & pricing proposal
messages:
From: Lucas Moreno <lucas@finopsanalytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finopsanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees (tokens/sec) and measurement approach

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. As we evaluate Redwood Dedicated for our inference tier, procurement wants clear throughput guarantees for budgeting and SLOs. Two asks from our side:

1) Can you commit to tokens/sec and requests/sec targets for a 1-year reserved GPU commit? We are primarily concerned about sustained throughput for a mixed sequence workload (median ~60 tokens, tail to 1024).
2) How do you measure these numbers? We need a repeatable methodology (warm vs cold cache, prefix/KV cache behavior, synthetic vs real prompt distribution) so our SREs can validate results before signing.

Also, we will likely request a discount tied to a 12-month reserved commitment; please include what discount tiers you can offer based on commit level (e.g., 2x, 5x, 10x baseline capacity).

Can you send a short measurement plan and an initial pricing/discount sketch? Looking to close purchase within 3 weeks if numbers align.

Thanks,
Lucas
Director of Platform Engineering
FinOpsAnalytics

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Moreno <lucas@finopsanalytics.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finopsanalytics.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees (tokens/sec) and measurement approach

Hi Lucas / Priya —

Appreciate the clear asks. High level answer up front, followed by an attached recommended test plan: redwood_throughput_test_plan_v1.xlsx (sent).

- Throughput guarantees (example for a 1yr reserved pool, per 8xA100-equivalent GPU pool):
  • Sustained tokens/sec (mixed workload, warm KV cache): 175k tokens/sec (p95 steady-state)
  • Requests/sec (avg 60-token responses): ~2,900 req/sec
  • Latency targets: p50 < 65ms per token, p95 < 320ms per token — subject to prompt length distribution and model family.

- Measurement methodology (summary):
  1) Use your representative prompt set (you can supply or use our synthetic mix that mirrors it).
  2) Warm run for 30 minutes to populate KV/prefix cache.
  3) Measure a 1-hour sustained window and report median/p95 tokens/sec and requests/sec.
  4) Run a cold-cache burst test (3x sustained for 5 minutes) to capture uncached behavior.
  5) Repeat across 3 independent runs on different days; we report the mean of the steady-state windows.

- Pricing / discount sketch:
  • Base on-demand Dedicated baseline price (list): $X per GPU-hour (see ROA_1yr_reserved_commit_terms.pdf).
  • 1yr reserved commitments: tiered discounts — 15% for 2x baseline, 25% for 5x baseline, 35% for 10x baseline.
  • We are open to blended options (capacity credits + committed throughput SLA) — we can map exact discounts once you confirm expected GPU-equivalent commit.

Markus (cc'd) will propose a more detailed measurement protocol and provide estimated GPU pool sizing for your target latency/throughput. Marissa will follow up on commercial terms and contract timing.

If agreeable, next step: (1) you share a small prompt sample (10–50 prompts) and 24hr traffic profile, (2) we schedule a 90-minute measurement run on a dedicated staging pool.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Moreno <lucas@finopsanalytics.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees (technical measurement plan)

Hi Lucas —

Quick technical addendum to Dylan's note with measurable steps and what we report back:

Measurement setup (detailed):
- Hardware baseline: 8xA100 equivalent (we map to your chosen instance type); results expressed per-8x pool.
- Model variant: specify exact model+quantization level. Different quant/ops change throughput by ~1.6x.
- Prompt distribution: we run three discrete mixes: 
  1) Short (median 40 tokens),
  2) Mixed (median 60 tokens) — matches your asks,
  3) Long-tail (median 220 tokens)
- Cache policy: three passes — cold (no KV), warm (KV warmed), and steady-state (continuous requests with prefix reuse).

Metrics we will publish in the report:
- tokens/sec (sustained window, per-GPU and pool-level),
- requests/sec (avg & p95),
- token-level latency distribution (p50,p90,p95,p99),
- GPU utilization and memory margins,
- Effective throughput per dollar (tokens per $).

Acceptance criteria for guaranteed SLA:
- We publish the steady-state p95 tokens/sec for the agreed prompt mix and model variant; SLA is defined as maintaining >= 95% of that published number over billing cycles, excluding scheduled maintenance and documented force majeure.

Notes on repeatability:
- We recommend you run your own verification using the same prompt set; we'll provide a runbook and a Dockerized driver for the benchmark.

I'll attach the driver and the exact csv/column schema in the Drive link. If you want, we can run an initial smoke test Thursday (your local time) and share the raw logs.

Thanks,
Markus
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finopsanalytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucas Moreno <lucas@finopsanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees (questions on pricing tie-ins)

Dylan / Markus —

Thanks for the plan. A couple of follow-ups from procurement before we schedule runs:

1) The discount tiers look reasonable, but procurement asks that the discount be conditional on a minimum effective throughput (your published p95 tokens/sec) rather than raw GPU count. Can you commit to tying the tier discount to the measured p95 throughput?
2) For SLA credits: what's the credit calculation if throughput drops below the published value? We need clear step-downs (e.g., <95% = X% credit, <90% = Y% credit).

Also please confirm if the warm-cache sustained window excludes traffic spikes that are driven by short-lived bursts (we'd like burst protection).

If you can provide the credit matrix and a short example calculation for a billing month, we can take this to legal and close the commercial talks.

Best,
Priya
VP of Procurement
FinOpsAnalytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finopsanalytics.com>, Lucas Moreno <lucas@finopsanalytics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees (commercial confirmation)

Hi Priya / Lucas —

Thanks — quick commercial confirmation below and we'll follow with a short legal-friendly term sheet.

Discount tie to throughput: yes, we can gate the discount tier on the measured steady-state p95 tokens/sec for the agreed prompt mix and model variant. We'll document the measurement harness and include the runbook in the contract appendix.

SLA credit matrix (example for monthly billing):
- If observed monthly steady-state throughput >= 95% of published p95: no credit.
- 90% <= observed < 95%: 10% credit on that month's Dedicated capacity invoice.
- 80% <= observed < 90%: 25% credit.
- observed < 80%: 50% credit + right to short-term remediation plan (technical triage + warm-up campaigns).

Burst exclusion: scheduled bursts and one-off traffic spikes are excluded if they exceed 5x baseline sustained for less than 10 minutes; our measurement windows (30min warm + 60min steady) will be used for the binding published numbers.

Next steps:
1) We'll finalize the term sheet and append the runbook to the SOW.
2) You provide the 50-sample prompt set and 24hr traffic shape.
3) We schedule the 90-minute run and produce the formal report.

I'll attach the draft term sheet to the Drive link and open a HubSpot record HS-93421 for the deal.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
